title: Swap a cracked crib block under a loaded beam
instruction: The red crib block under the beam is cracked. Swap it for the green block and put the red one in the grey tray. The beam must not drop or move.
context: Riggers and millwrights (O*NET 49-9096, 49-9044) crib raised loads, and OSHA 29 CFR 1926.600(a)(3)(i) requires raised parts to be blocked or cribbed. A damaged crib is never pulled until its replacement is set under the load, within a millimetre of it, so the load can only settle, not fall; the same holds for flight hardware on support stands during integration. Unlike leaving a prop in place (TK-XGA43V) or holding a load by hand while a stated order withdraws its support (TK-3F2PGK), here nothing holds the beam, the order is never stated, and the new crib must go in beside the old one first, the reverse of the remove-then-fit order of a module swap. The green crib is 1 mm lower, so it slides in with the red one still there. Pulled first, the red crib lets the beam pivot on the pier and its free end falls 40 mm, an 11.5 degree tilt that scores 0 for the whole trial. Physics, not a rule, punishes the wrong plan. 1 g tabletop analogue; no microgravity is claimed.
setup: Table coordinates in metres: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left from the midline, z up from the table top; the right arm's base is at (0, -0.305). The task is laid out in front of the right arm; the left arm rests at its ready pose. Fixed, painted steel, dark grey (sRGB 0.30, 0.31, 0.33): a pier block 80 (x) x 60 (y) x 40 (z) mm centred at (0.290, -0.310), spanning y -0.340 to -0.280; on its top, two saddle lips 10 x 60 x 20 mm centred at x 0.2645 and 0.3155, y -0.310, their inner faces 41 mm apart. Loose: the beam, a 6061 aluminium rectangular tube 40 (x) x 260 (y) x 20 (z) mm with 2 mm walls and an oak plug 12 mm deep in each end, 168 g in all, aluminium grey (sRGB 0.55, 0.57, 0.60), lying along y centred at (0.290, -0.210) with its underside 40 mm up, spanning y -0.340 to -0.080 and x 0.270 to 0.310. Its right end rests on the pier between the lips, 0.5 mm from each, which stop it sliding along x or turning more than about 1 degree; nothing holds its left end down. The red crib: an oak block 100 (x) x 30 (y) x 40 (z) mm, 84 g, painted red (sRGB 0.80, 0.15, 0.12), centred at (0.270, -0.110) with its long axis along x; it spans x 0.220 to 0.320 under the beam's left end and stands 50 mm proud of the beam toward the arm. The green crib: an oak block 100 x 30 x 39 mm, 82 g, painted green (sRGB 0.20, 0.60, 0.25), lying on the table along x centred at (0.150, -0.185); 1 mm lower than the red crib, it fits under the beam with 1 mm to spare. The beam's weight, 1.65 N, acts at y -0.210, midway between the pier and the red crib, so each carries 0.82 N; the pier's inner edge is at y -0.280. Fixed, grey polypropylene (sRGB 0.45, 0.45, 0.47): a scrap tray centred at (0.150, -0.400), a 3 mm floor 130 x 70 mm inside four walls 4 mm thick and 15 mm tall (138 x 78 mm outside). Distances from the right base: the green crib's near end 0.16 m, the red crib's near end 0.30 m, the tray 0.18 m. To build it: bolt or tape the steel block straight to the table, so its top is 40.0 mm above the surface the cribs stand on, and screw two 10 x 20 mm steel flat bars 60 mm long to its top; cut the beam from 40 x 20 x 2 mm aluminium tube and plug its ends; plane two oak blocks to 40.0 and 39.0 mm thick and paint them; tape a polypropylene tray to its mark.
scoring: In simulation the scorer reads object poses on every control step; on real arms the record is read from the trial video and the end state from a top photo, a steel rule and a phone level. Disturbance record: the beam must never tilt more than 2.5 degrees from level (its own vertical axis to the world vertical) nor have its centre move more than 6 mm in any direction from where it rests. It is checked on every step and cleared only when a new trial starts: at the first scored step, or when the simulator's reset puts every body back on its mark, seen as a body's centre jumping more than 15 mm in one step while it reports under 10 mm/s before and after, which no push, fall or slide can do in one 50 ms step. Once tripped, the trial scores 0 whatever the end state, so a beam that dropped and was lifted back, or was shoved or lifted and put back before either crib moved, still scores 0. A non-finite pose trips it. Green seated: at rest (under 10 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s), flat (its 39 mm axis within 3 degrees of vertical, either face up), long axis within 10 degrees of x either way round, lowest corner within 2 mm of the table, centre at x 0.255 to 0.325 and y -0.205 to -0.090: across at least 35 mm of the beam's 40 mm width and under its left half, the red crib's own place included. Red out: at rest with no part of its outline, seen from above, inside the beam's outline where the beam now lies (x 0.270 to 0.310, y -0.340 to -0.080 at rest). Red binned: at rest with its centre inside the tray walls (x 0.085 to 0.215, y -0.435 to -0.365) and its lowest corner within 3 mm of the tray floor. Score with the record clear: 0 unless green is seated (this includes the start); 0.4 green seated; 0.7 green seated and red out; 1.0 green seated, red binned and the beam at rest within 1.5 degrees of level. Success, which ends the trial, is the 1.0 condition held for 1 s. Physics: pull the red crib before the green one is under the beam and the beam pivots on the pier's inner edge until its left end meets the table, 11.5 degrees, which trips the record. Slide the green crib in first, beside the red one, and the beam settles onto it when the red crib comes out, about 0.5 degrees. Lifting the free end more than about 11 mm, or dragging the beam, also trips the record. Either crib may be slid, pushed or carried. A green crib crosswise, on its side, tilted, held up or moving is not seated; a red crib partly under the beam, on it or moving is not out. On the real rig a trial in which the pier, lips or tray move more than 2 mm scores 0, and the photo after the arms park decides, since the simulated scorer cannot see the grippers.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Lift the beam off, set the red crib on its mark centred at (0.270, -0.110) with its long axis along x, lay the beam back level on the pier between the lips and on the red crib, then lay the green crib on its mark at (0.150, -0.185) and empty the tray. The pier, lips and tray do not move; check them against their marks. Run with -E object_jitter=0: the layout and the open-loop demo depend on it.
fidelity: Approximate: rigid primitives with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic) and matte colours. The plugged tube is a solid box of the same outer size and mass; the crack is colour only and no crib crushes. The load is 1.65 N, not tonnes, so a drop shows as tilt, not damage. The pier, lips and tray are fixed colliders. Earth gravity on a bench, where this work is done.
